correctness.rationale: The Steingrimsson complex is the link of the graphical arrangement in the mean-zero unit sphere, not the similarly named cyclic coloring complex. Each acyclic orientation corresponds to one convex spherical chamber; the relative top homology H_{n-2}(S_n,X_n;Z) is its integral orientation-twisted free chamber lattice. The ambient sphere class embeds as the primitive diagonal sum, yielding a torsion-free coaugmentation *quotient*, not the generally nonisomorphic augmentation kernel. A rotation fixes 2^d-2 chamber orientations, and a reflection fixes 0 or 2^{n/2} according to its edge-orbit reversals; multiply the resulting count minus 1 by the vertex-permutation sign. For fixed loci, coordinate equality inside a vertex orbit forces the entire fixed sphere into the arrangement; otherwise the orbit graph is C_d or a path, giving the asserted spherical wedges. The quotient rank is the rational average. Independently enumerated every acyclic orientation and all dihedral vertex maps for n=3..12 and verified both axis sign patterns and character averages, including n=8 invariant rank 13. No integral quotient homology is inferred from rational transfer.

originality.rationale: Ordinary homotopy concentration and number of acyclic orientations are classical from Jonsson and Hersh–Swartz; the entire signed dihedral integral lattice, reflection-fixed geometry and full quotient ranks are separate. Hanlon 2008 Hodge decomposition partitions top homology by chromatic-polynomial coefficients, but accessible abstract/secondary article does not state a polygon-label permutation module or fixed subspace classification; complete text remains inaccessible. Macauley–Mortveit use source-to-sink equivalence on orientations, not the relabeling action on chamber chains. Braun–Crown Rundell have signed-graph hyperoctahedral Hodge operators on chain slots, not this D_n label action. The natural arrangement chamber argument makes the statement plausible and relatively elementary, but an explicit integral full-family representation remains a meaningful exact refinement; an older equivariant statement is a material residual priority risk.

value.rationale: The explicit integral Z[D_n]-module holds for a canonical infinite graph family and retains extension information that is lost under rationalization. The fixed point loci depend sharply on the axis type (at n=8 S^2 versus a wedge of 15 copies), a distinction not determined by ordinary sphere rank. Uniform full quotient rational Betti counts offer a useful symmetry invariant. It is more than renaming a standard chamber count because it identifies the actual integral equivariant cokernel and fixed geometry.
